title: Sliding Window
summary: Maintain a contiguous range of the array and slide/resize it incrementally instead of recomputing from scratch.
explanation: Sliding window solves problems about contiguous subarrays or substrings by keeping a running window [start, end] and updating its running state (sum, count, set of characters, etc.) incrementally as the window moves, instead of recomputing that state from scratch for every possible window.
A fixed-size window (e.g. "max sum of any k consecutive elements") slides one step at a time: add the element entering on the right, remove the element leaving on the left, and compare.

A variable-size window (e.g. "smallest subarray with sum >= target") grows by moving the right edge forward until a condition is met, then shrinks by moving the left edge forward while the condition still holds — recording the best window found along the way. Each edge only ever moves forward, so the total work is O(n) even though it looks like two nested loops.
whenToUse: The problem asks for a contiguous subarray or substring (not any subset).
You're optimizing (max/min/count) some property — sum, length, number of distinct characters — over all contiguous windows.
A brute-force approach recomputes the same overlapping range's sum/count repeatedly.
Elements only need to be added or removed from the ends of the current window, not the middle.
spaceComplexity: O(1) to O(k), depending on what the window tracks
